Original Requirements: Build the Volopa OOP (Out-of-Pocket) Expenses API System using Laravel 10+ with PHP 8.2+. Three modules: 1. User Management & Permissions — RBAC via user_feature_permission with delegation hierarchy, 2. Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload — synchronous validation, async background sync, 3. Single Expense Data Capturing — CRUD with FX conversion and flexible metadata
Product Goals: Enable comprehensive out-of-pocket expense tracking for Volopa users
Provide flexible role-based permission management with delegation capabilities
Support efficient bulk expense entry through CSV batch upload
Deliver accurate FX conversion for multi-currency expenses
Ensure data integrity through validation and atomic operations
Maintain security through proper authentication and authorization
Provide scalable metadata capture for expense categorization
Enable seamless integration with existing Volopa platform services
User Stories: As a Primary Admin, I want to enable OOP Expense feature for my organization so employees can track business expenses
As a Primary Admin, I want to delegate expense management rights to other users so I can distribute workload
As an Admin with management rights, I want to create expenses for my managed users so I can handle their submissions
As an employee, I want to create single expense entries with receipt attachments so I can record my business expenses
As an employee, I want automatic FX conversion when entering foreign currency expenses so amounts are normalized to company currency
As an Admin, I want to upload CSV files with bulk expenses so I can efficiently enter historical or recurring expenses
As a user, I want to see detailed validation errors for failed CSV uploads so I can correct and resubmit my data
As a system administrator, I want to configure expense sources for my organization so users have appropriate categorization options
As an employee, I want to attach metadata like categories and tracking codes to my expenses so they integrate with existing financial processes
As a user, I want to view and edit my own expenses in draft status so I can refine entries before submission
As an approver, I want to review and approve submitted expenses so I can maintain financial control
As an Admin, I want to receive notifications when batch uploads complete so I know when to review new entries
Competitive Analysis: Expensify: Strong mobile app, receipt OCR, but limited delegation hierarchy
Concur SAP: Enterprise-grade permissions, complex workflow, but heavy UI
Rydoo: Good multi-currency support, clean interface, limited bulk operations
Zoho Expense: Comprehensive features, good integrations, but complex permission model
Receipt Bank (now Dext): Excellent receipt processing, limited expense workflow
Chrome River: Strong approval workflows, enterprise focus, outdated interface
Abacus (now Emburse): Real-time expense tracking, good UX, limited customization

Requirement Analysis: The Volopa OOP Expenses system is designed as a comprehensive API-first solution that integrates with existing Volopa infrastructure. The system must handle three distinct but interconnected modules: permission management with delegation hierarchy, bulk CSV processing with atomic validation, and single expense entry with real-time FX conversion. Key technical constraints include OAuth2 authentication, multi-tenant data scoping, 200-row CSV limits, and 30-day FX rate lookback. The system leverages existing Volopa services for authentication, FX conversion, file storage, and notifications while maintaining strict data integrity through Laravel transactions and comprehensive validation rules. The permission model supports four existing user roles with granular delegation capabilities, allowing Primary Admins to distribute expense management responsibilities while maintaining approval workflows.
Requirement Pool: Implement OAuth2-authenticated API endpoints for CRUD operations on pocket expenses with proper role-based access control
Build user_feature_permission table and delegation system allowing Primary Admins to grant/revoke expense management rights
Create CSV batch upload with synchronous validation (max 200 rows) and atomic all-or-nothing expense creation
Implement real-time FX conversion integration with 2-second debounce and 30-day rate lookback for multi-currency expenses
Build flexible metadata system linking expenses to categories, tracking codes, projects, and additional fields
Implement expense source configuration allowing clients to manage custom source types with soft delete support
Create comprehensive error handling with detailed CSV validation feedback and downloadable error reports
UI Design draft: API-first design with no direct UI components. The system provides RESTful JSON endpoints for frontend consumption. Key API groups include: /api/v1/pocket-expenses for CRUD operations with pagination and filtering; /api/v1/pocket-expenses/batch-upload for CSV processing with validation feedback; /api/v1/user-feature-permissions for delegation management; /api/v1/expense-sources for source configuration. All endpoints return consistent JSON responses with proper HTTP status codes (201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 422). Error responses follow standardized format with field-level validation details. File uploads use multipart/form-data with size and type validation. FX conversion endpoints provide real-time rate lookup with commission calculation. API documentation follows OpenAPI specification with clear request/response schemas and authentication requirements.
Anything UNCLEAR: Two unresolved decisions require clarification: 1) The notification channel for batch upload completion (in-app, email, or combination) needs to be specified for complete implementation. 2) The exact query pattern for checking if a client has the OOP feature enabled through the existing ClientFeatures model needs to be defined (e.g., feature_id = 16 lookup). The FX service integration approach (reuse existing platform service vs new implementation for 30-day lookback + commission calculation) also needs confirmation, though the YAML suggests platform reuse is preferred.
